questions.q: In function add(a: number, b: number): number { ... }, where does the return type annotation go?
options: Before the function keyword
After each parameter name
After the parameter list's closing parenthesis, before the function body
Inside the function body as a comment
questions.explain: The return type annotation follows the closing parenthesis of the parameter list and precedes the opening brace of the function body.

questions.q: If you omit the return type annotation on a simple function, what does TypeScript typically do?
options: It assumes the return type is any
It throws a compile error demanding an explicit return type
It infers the return type automatically based on what the function actually returns
It treats the function as returning void regardless of its return statement
questions.explain: TypeScript's type inference can usually determine a function's return type on its own without an explicit annotation.

questions.q: What's the difference between function connect(url: string, timeoutMs?: number) and function connect(url: string, timeoutMs: number = 5000)?
options: There is no difference
The first makes timeoutMs optional (undefined if omitted); the second also makes it optional but fills in 5000 if omitted
The second makes timeoutMs required
The first assigns 5000 automatically; the second does not
questions.explain: Both make the parameter optional for the caller, but a default value actually substitutes a real value (5000) when the argument is omitted, rather than leaving it undefined.

questions.q: Given let onConfirm: (txHash: string) => void;, what happens if you assign a function with an extra parameter to onConfirm?
options: It's allowed silently with no error
TypeScript flags it as a type error at the assignment
It only errors once onConfirm is actually called
JavaScript ignores extra parameters so no checking occurs
questions.explain: A function type describes the exact parameter types and return type required; assigning a mismatched function is caught immediately as a compile-time error.

questions.q: Which of these is a real-world example of a typed callback mentioned in this lesson?
options: A CSS class name
An array's .map() method handing you an already-typed callback based on the array's element type
A string concatenation operator
A variable declared with const
questions.explain: Array methods like .map() infer and type their callback's parameter based on the array's element type, which is one common place typed function callbacks show up.
